page.title: Turntable With Preamp: Line Output of 5 Built-In Phono Preamps Compared (2026)
page.h1: Turntable with a built-in preamp: how much signal each one sends to your speakers
page.desc: Five turntables with a built-in phono preamp, compared by their rated line output: AT-LP70X 252 mV, AT-LP120XUSB 240 mV, Sony PS-LX3BT 180 mV, Fluance RT81 and RT81+ 140 mV.
page.answer: Short answer. A turntable with a built-in phono preamp plugs straight into powered speakers on its LINE setting. The best in 2026 is the Audio-Technica AT-LP70X: its preamp puts out 252 mV, about 5 dB more than the Fluance RT81's 140 mV, so the speakers need less volume.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • AT-LP70X vs Fluance RT81: 20·log10(252 ÷ 140) = 5.1 dB, or 1.8× the voltage. Through the same powered speakers at the same volume setting, the AT-LP70X plays about 5 dB louder.
  • Against the −10 dBV (316 mV) consumer line reference: AT-LP70X 20·log10(252 ÷ 316) = −2.0 dB; RT81 and RT81+ 20·log10(140 ÷ 316) = −7.1 dB. Every deck here is below that reference, and the Fluance pair is furthest below it.
  • Gain check: AT-LP70X 252 ÷ 4.0 = 63×, and 20·log10(63) = 36 dB, matching Audio-Technica's stated gain. Sony PS-LX3BT 180 ÷ 2.5 = 72×, about 37 dB, so its preamp works hard but starts from a weaker 2.5 mV cartridge.
  • Price: the RT81 costs $299.99 − $249 = $50.99 more than the AT-LP70X in Black/Bronze. The AT-LP120XUSB costs $399 − $249 = $150 more.
Your setupBest fit
Powered speakers or a soundbar AUX input, simplest setupAudio-Technica AT-LP70X
Manual play and an adjustable tonearm, or a separate phono preamp laterFluance RT81 (expect to turn the volume up by about 5 dB)
Recording records to a computer, direct driveAudio-Technica AT-LP120XUSB
Bluetooth to an aptX Adaptive speaker or headphonesSony PS-LX3BT

How loud a built-in preamp is, and why it matters

A phono cartridge puts out only a few millivolts. The built-in preamp applies RIAA equalization and amplifies that to line level, so a deck switched to LINE can go into powered speakers or an amplifier's AUX input. Passive speakers still need an amplifier. If your amplifier has its own PHONO input, set the turntable to PHONO so the signal isn't equalized twice. The rated line output tells you how much signal arrives at the speakers. A lower figure means the speakers' volume sits higher for the same loudness, which matters most with speakers or soundbars whose AUX input has little gain to spare.

Audio-Technica rates the AT-LP70X and AT-LP120XUSB at 1 kHz and 5 cm/sec. Sony rates the PS-LX3BT at 1 kHz but does not say which of its three gain-switch settings the 180 mV figure uses. Fluance gives 140 mV for both the RT81 and RT81+ with no test condition. The RT81+'s cartridge is stronger (4.0 mV against 3.5 mV), but Fluance still rates its line output at the same 140 mV. Reviewing the RT81 for Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity in 2016, John E. Johnson, Jr. listed "Higher output (0.5 volts) from the phono preamplifier" under "Would Like To See".

Line output is a loudness figure, not a sound-quality verdict. Fluance states signal-to-noise of 67 dB or more, A-weighted. Audio-Technica states more than 55 dB for the AT-LP70X without naming a weighting, so the two noise figures can't be compared directly. One limit applies only to the Sony: on its Japanese product page, Sony says TVs, smartphones and PCs cannot receive the PS-LX3BT's Bluetooth stream, and that for Bluetooth-only use the rear OUTPUT SELECT switch must be set to LINE.

Not recommended

Don't buy the Fluance RT81+ for a louder built-in preamp. It costs $50 more than the RT81 ($349.99 against $299.99), and Fluance rates its line output at the same 140 mV. The extra money pays for the AT-VM95E cartridge, not for more signal at the LINE output. Also check the model name: Fluance's RT82 sells for the same $349.99 but has no built-in preamp at all.
